question: The income of Raman is ₹34,000. He saves 5.5% of his income. If his income increases by 17% and expenditure increases by 50%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net change in Savings = Increase in Income − Increase in Expenditure

Income = 100%, Initial Expenditure = 100% − 5.5% = 94.5%

Change in Savings = 17% of Income − 50% of Initial Expenditure

⇒ Change % = 17% − (50% of 94.5%) = 17% − 47.25% = −30.25%

⇒ Change in Savings = −30.25% of 34,000 = −10,285

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹10,285.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Original State (100% = ₹34,000) Total Income = 100% Expenditure = 94.5% 
• Sav = 5.5% New State (After % Changes) New Income = 117% New Expenditure = 141.75% 
• Shortfall (−24.75%) 

**Given:**

Income of Raman = ₹34,000

Initial Savings = 5.5% of Income

Income increases by 17%

Expenditure increases by 50%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Savings = (5.5 ÷ 100) × 34,000 = ₹1,870

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 34,000 − 1,870 = ₹32,130

⇒ New Income = 34,000 × (100 + 17)% = 34,000 × 1.17 = ₹39,780

⇒ New Expenditure = 32,130 × (100 + 50)% = 32,130 × 1.50 = ₹48,195

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure

⇒ New Savings = 39,780 − 48,195 = −₹8,415

⇒ Change in Savings = New Savings − Initial Savings

⇒ Change in Savings = −8,415 − 1,870 = −10,285

Since the change in savings is negative, the overall savings will decrease by ₹10,285.

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹10,285.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure Relation

Income = Expenditure + Savings. The sum of the changes in expenditure and savings will always be exactly equal to the total change in income.

Percentage Change

Percentage Change = (New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value × 100. A negative result inherently denotes a percentage decrease.

Successive Percentage

When a base value undergoes sequential changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is evaluated directly as: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.
